analysis: The only change in this PR is a single documentation line in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1846, the `stop` row of the sampling-parameters table). It now says stop strings are matched on held-back detokenised text via `StopHoldback`, that GPT-OSS sets `stopStringScope` to the Harmony `final` message (`ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`) so analysis and tool-call frames never match, and that the reported sequence replays the same scope. No code, configuration, key handling, cache storage, attestation, coordinator protocol or authorization surface is modified, so no threat model asset, trust boundary or mitigation in the supplied context changes (A-001, TB-002, TB-007, T-041 and the others). I read the rest of the supplied documentation (units 14 and 15) and did not find anything that contradicts the new line. The line does describe a behavior (scoping stop matching to the final message) whose implementation I could not see. If that implementation mishandles the scope, the likely effects are incorrect output truncation or stop-sequence leakage of analysis content, which is an output-correctness or integrity concern (related to T-007) and not a new confidentiality or authorization regression. The visible evidence does not establish such a defect. Next-pass questions, none with a security conclusion: whether `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope` and `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift` actually implement the documented behavior, and whether the scoped replay of the reported sequence cannot expose hidden analysis or tool-call text to the consumer. These are outside the supplied evidence, so I record them as an unverified contract and raise no finding.
